# graxia

> A Bun-native GraphQL server engine: typed plugins, graphql 17 and GraphQL over HTTP. `@graxia/core` ships the HTTP transport, plugins, context and cancellation, error masking, subscriptions over server-sent events and WebSocket, `@defer` and `@stream`, a typed PubSub, a key-value cache contract, in-process `execute` and a test client. `@graxia/redis` swaps the PubSub and the cache for Redis and adds a shared field rate limit. Trusted documents (manifests, `documentId`, automatic persisted queries, strict mode) are built; telemetry runs on `@softistx/telemetry` (optional peer), and `@graxia/mcp` serves it to agents over MCP.

## @graxia/core

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/README.md): The Bun-native GraphQL server engine: typed plugins, graphql 17, GraphQL over HTTP, with no adapter layer.
- [Ready for agents: `@graxia/core/agent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/agent.md): A schema an AI agent can read and act on needs four things: what each field requires, the limits of each input, the errors each field may return, and a `fix`…
- [Codegen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/codegen.md): graphql-codegen's `typescript` and `typescript-resolvers` plugins type every resolver from your SDL.
- [Context, cancellation and shutdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/context.md): Every operation gets its own context, its own cancellation signal, and is tracked so that `dispose()` can drain it.
- [Errors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/errors.md): A client sees two kinds of errors. **Exposed** errors are the ones you chose to show: their message, `extensions.code` and `extensions.fix` reach the response.
- [GraphQL over HTTP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/http.md): `createGraxia` serves a schema over GraphQL over HTTP on Bun.
- [`@defer` and `@stream`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/incremental.md): Incremental delivery sends the parts of a result as they become ready: a query with `@defer` or `@stream` answers a first payload at once, then more payloads…
- [Limits and caches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/limits-and-caches.md): Before a document is parsed, graxia bounds it; once parsed, it keeps the result.
- [Migrating from `@alxia/graphql`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/migrating-from-alxia-graphql.md): `@alxia/graphql` mounts GraphQL Yoga on an alxia app.
- [Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/plugins.md): A plugin is a plain object with a `name` and the hooks it needs. `definePlugin` types it.
- [Production](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/production.md): A checklist to ship a graxia server: what `NODE_ENV=production` changes, a complete configuration, what to set behind a proxy, how to shut down, and what to…
- [PubSub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/pubsub.md): `createPubSub` is a typed publish/subscribe for subscription resolvers, with the same shape as GraphQL Yoga's `createPubSub`: the same topic typing, the same…
- [Rate limiting fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/rate-limiting.md): `fieldRateLimit` limits how often a client may select chosen fields, counted across aliases and fragments. It is a plugin: nothing changes until you add it.
- [Schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/schema.md): `createSchema` builds a plain graphql `GraphQLSchema` from SDL and resolvers. Any `GraphQLSchema` works wherever graxia expects one; this is only a helper.
- [Security: CSRF, origins, introspection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/security.md): Three defaults protect a server that browsers can reach. Each has an option; none replaces authentication.
- [Subscriptions over server-sent events](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/subscriptions.md): `createGraxia` serves subscriptions over server-sent events (SSE), in the **distinct connections mode** of the `graphql-sse` protocol: one HTTP request, one…
- [Telemetry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/telemetry.md): graxia emits spans for each request, parse, validation and operation, and optionally for each resolver, on `@softistx/telemetry`.
- [Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/testing.md): Two tools, no socket: `graxia.execute` runs an operation in process, and `@graxia/core/testing` talks to `graxia.fetch` with real HTTP semantics.
- [Trusted documents and persisted queries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/trusted-documents.md): In production a GraphQL endpoint should run only the documents your own clients ship.
- [File uploads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/uploads.md): `@graxia/core` accepts the GraphQL multipart request spec (`operations`, `map`, one part per file). It is off by default.
- [Subscriptions over WebSocket](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/guide/websocket.md): `createGraxia` serves GraphQL over WebSocket in the `graphql-transport-ws` protocol (the one the `graphql-ws` client speaks), on Bun's native WebSocket.
- [Troubleshooting: file uploads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/troubleshooting-uploads.md): Every message of File uploads, headed by the text the server sends. The rest is in Troubleshooting.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/core/docs/troubleshooting.md): File upload messages are in Troubleshooting: file uploads.

## @graxia/envelop

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/envelop/README.md): Run Envelop plugins inside graxia with one import and one call.
- [Running Envelop plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/envelop/docs/guide/envelop.md): `fromEnvelop(plugins, options?)` takes the list you would give `envelop()` and returns one graxia plugin.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/envelop/docs/troubleshooting.md): The errors a consumer can hit, headed by the message as it appears. All are a `GraxiaConfigError` thrown by `fromEnvelop` at boot, unless said otherwise.

## @graxia/graphiql

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/graphiql/README.md): The GraphiQL 4 page for graxia, bundled at build time: it runs under a strict content security policy, with no CDN, no external font and no analytics.
- [Apollo Sandbox](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/graphiql/docs/guide/apollo-sandbox.md): `apolloSandbox()` is a graxia plugin that serves Apollo Sandbox from the GraphQL endpoint, pointed at that same endpoint.
- [GraphiQL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/graphiql/docs/guide/graphiql.md): `graphiql()` is a graxia plugin that serves the GraphiQL 4 page from the GraphQL endpoint itself.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/graphiql/docs/troubleshooting.md): The browser blocked the script or the style under the CSP, or never received them. Open the console: a `Refused to load…` message names the directive.

## @graxia/mcp

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/README.md): A Model Context Protocol server for a graxia API.
- [OAuth resource server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/guide/auth.md): With `auth`, `@graxia/mcp` is an OAuth 2.1 **resource server** (MCP authorization spec, RFC 9728, RFC 8707): it accepts bearer access tokens, it never issues…
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/guide/getting-started.md): `createMcp(graxia, options)` reads the schema and the body limit from the instance (`graxia.schema`, `graxia.limits.bodyBytes`, `@graxia/core` 0.5), so…
- [Persisted operations as typed tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/guide/operations.md): Give `createMcp` the operations your clients already persist and each one becomes an MCP tool: a name, a description, a JSON Schema for its arguments (from…
- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/guide/security.md): Set `auth` and `@graxia/mcp` is an OAuth resource server: bearer tokens, scopes, protected resource metadata (the auth guide).
- [Tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/guide/tools.md): Every tool sees the schema as the caller may see it: with `can`, a field behind `@needs` the caller lacks does not exist for them (it is neither described nor…
- [Troubleshooting auth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/troubleshooting-auth.md): The answers of `auth` (the auth guide) and its boot errors, each headed by the message or code you see. Everything else is in troubleshooting.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/mcp/docs/troubleshooting.md): Each entry is headed by the message or code you see. The 401, 403 and 503 answers of `auth` and its boot errors are in troubleshooting auth.

## @graxia/redis

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/redis/README.md): Redis PubSub, cache and field rate limit for graxia, on `@softistx/redis` (one shared client per URI, one reconnecting subscriber connection, server-timed…
- [Redis PubSub, cache and field rate limit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/redis/docs/guide/redis.md): Both adapters take `{ url }` or `{ client }`, never both (see troubleshooting).
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/softistx/graxia/develop/packages/redis/docs/troubleshooting.md): The errors a consumer can hit, headed by the message as it appears.
